request.tone: quiet suspense mystery about listening and estrangement; violence mild, scariness moderate, peril moderate
request.note: catalog book read blind; no request exists

pitch.hero: Wren Callahan, a sleepless teen grieving her radio-operator grandfather
pitch.want: to find who is behind the numbers loop on his old radio and why it never stops
pitch.obstacle: a dark relay station, a coded loop, and a countdown that ends at twenty to midnight tonight
pitch.stake: Kell Alder's thirty-year call to his daughter Marin, erased unheard when his station's cell dies
pitch.ending_kind: reunions, saved tapes or a message carried on; setbacks of delay, force, caution or false promise

wren.name: Wren Callahan
wren.want: to answer the voice in the static before it ends
wren.voice: close third past; dry, careful, brave in small steps; tested on acting before she is sure

grandpa.name: Grandpa Callahan
grandpa.role: Wren's late grandfather, a radio operator
grandpa.want: for someone to answer Kell Alder
grandpa.voice: present only through logbooks, notes, letters and his square capitals

kell.name: Kell Alder
kell.role: the relay's last operator, sender of the loop
kell.want: to call his daughter home, then let her be
kell.voice: old, tired, formal on tape; gruff and gentle in person

marin.name: Marin Alder
marin.role: Kell's estranged daughter, the voice reading the numbers
marin.want: unstated; she never quite stopped listening
marin.voice: careful vowels, bored and fond as a girl; wary as a woman

okafor.name: Mrs. Okafor
okafor.role: net-mender at the marina, Kell's quiet keeper
okafor.want: for somebody finally to hear the loop
okafor.voice: spare, sharp as fishhooks, kind underneath

pell.name: Mr. Pell
pell.want: not to hand a man's name to a child at midnight

ruiz.name: Ruiz
ruiz.role: former relay man who stayed across the bay
ruiz.want: to end thirty years of two old men not talking

kell_sister.name: Kell's sister
kell_sister.want: for someone to reach Marin in time

truth.question: Who is sending the numbers loop, to whom, and why is it ending?
truth.statement: The loop comes from Relay KX on the headland, which the county closed thirty years ago. Its last operator, Kell Alder, stayed on and every night sends a recording of his daughter Marin reading the station numbers, opened by M in Morse, after a quarrel drove her away; he vowed to keep a channel open until she answered. The station's only power cell is failing, and the loop is a countdown: at twenty to midnight tonight a final tape plays his goodbye and then erases everything.

wren_callahan.text: The hero is Wren Callahan, a girl who cannot sleep.

attic_shortwave.text: Her late grandfather's shortwave radio sits in the attic, and Wren climbs up to switch it on.

wren_listens_nightly_week.text: Wren has switched the radio on every night for a week.

loop_numbers_voice.text: Out of the hiss comes a loop: a young woman's flat, careful voice reading a string of numbers over and over.

loop_descending_tone.text: After the numbers a slow tone counts downward and resets, and the cycle starts again from the top.

spare_battery_on_shelf.text: On the attic shelf sits his spare battery, wrapped in a rag and labeled JUST IN CASE.

headset_on_hook.text: His heavy operator's headset hangs on a hook, cracked leather pads, the name Callahan inked inside the band.

headset_hears_room.text: Grandpa swore the headset could let you hear the room behind a voice.

grandpa_died_year_ago.text: Her grandfather died about a year ago.

wren_never_touched_his_things.text: Before tonight Wren had never touched the battery or the headset; she dusted around them for a year.

wren_had_handled_his_things.text: Wren had handled her grandfather's battery and headset before tonight.

wren_only_attic_visitor.text: Wren is the only one who still comes up to the attic.

one_thing_bargain.text: Wren allows herself to take down one thing of his, and only one.

battery_in_pack.text: Wren took her grandfather's spare battery and carries it in the bottom of her pack.

battery_left_on_shelf.text: Grandpa's spare battery is still wrapped in its rag on the attic shelf; Wren did not bring it.

headset_taken.text: Wren took her grandfather's headset off its hook and wears it at the radio.

headset_deepens_signal.text: Through the headset the hiss deepens like a big room and the woman's voice comes very close.

grandpa_taught_coords.text: Grandpa taught Wren to plot numbers as coordinates on graph paper.

relay_station_headland.text: An old relay station stands on the headland and has been dark as long as Wren can remember.

grandpa_kept_logbook.text: Grandpa kept a logbook of everything he heard on the radio, every night for forty years.

three_leads.text: Three leads pull at Wren: plot the numbers as coordinates, go to the relay station, or find Grandpa's logbook.

loop_from_relay.text: The loop is transmitted from the old relay station on the headland.

two_coords_harbor_tower.text: Two of the number pairs plot to real places: the working harbor and the old water tower on the headland ridge.

wren_has_graph_paper.text: Wren carries the graph paper with her plotted crosses.

wren_has_handheld.text: Wren has a handheld radio clipped to her belt, its battery light already amber.

harbor_layout.text: At the harbor are the lit harbormaster's hut, the tide-gauge shed said to be shut for years, and the pier notice-board.

notice_card.text: A fresh index card pinned mid-board gives a frequency and the words: if you hear the loop, it is real.

card_freq_matches_loop.text: The card's frequency matches the loop exactly.

card_ink_fresh.text: The card's ink is still damp; it has been up less than a day.

signal_strongest_north.text: On the card's frequency the signal swells only toward the north, along the shore to the headland.

wren_has_notice_card.text: Wren has the index card in her back pocket.

card_replaced_by_someone.text: Someone in town replaces the pier card every time it blows away, and has for years.

loop_went_silent_missed.text: The loop went silent for good before Wren could reach or answer it.

mr_pell.text: Mr. Pell is the harbormaster, curious and kindly at midnight.

county_closed_relay.text: The county stopped funding and shut down the relay station years ago.

pell_withholds_name.text: Mr. Pell could name the man keeping the signal going but will not tell a child.

shed_receiver_listening.text: Inside the shut tide-gauge shed a small receiver blinks in time with the loop, its frequency on a strip of tape.

relay_kx_name.text: The relay station is called Relay KX (Station KX).

shed_is_ear.text: The shed receiver is only a listening post rigged to catch a signal from further out on the headland.

grandpa_marked_dial.text: Grandpa marked the loop's frequency on the attic dial with a pencil tick worn dark by years of use.

grandpa_never_told.text: Grandpa heard the loop for years and never told anyone about it.

tower_rebroadcasts.text: Something on the ridge water tower catches the signal and throws it on.

tower_ladder_and_box.text: The tower has a flaking uncaged maintenance ladder and a steel service box at its foot.

wren_froze_on_ladder.text: Wren froze on the eighth rung of the tower ladder and climbed down shaking.

cable_to_relay.text: A cable runs from the tower along the ridge, post after post, to the relay station on the point.

stenciled_arrows.text: Faded stenciled arrows on the pad point along the ridge path toward the headland.

tower_is_repeater.text: A tag reads KX RELAY, HEADLAND, DO NOT DISCONNECT; the tower is only a repeater for the headland transmitter.

wren_skinned_knuckle.text: Wren skinned a knuckle prying open the service box.

arrows_reflective.text: Each arrow has a dab of reflective paint, marking the path for someone walking it in the dark.

relay_lit.text: The relay station is not dark: a red lamp burns on the mast and one window in the low building is lit yellow.

fence_open_side.text: The fence does not run along the cliff side, so Wren can reach the lit window.

relay_gate_chained.text: The relay station's road ends at a chained gate.

wren_has_bicycle.text: Wren rides her bicycle out to the headland.

fence_gap.text: The chain-link fence has peeled back from a post, leaving a gap.

wren_has_phone.text: Wren has her phone in her jacket pocket.

relay_maintained.text: Inside the compound the weeds are cut, new cable is stored and a generator ticks over; the place is tended.

wren_scraped_elbow.text: Wren scraped her elbow on the fence wire.

man_with_mug_photo.text: Wren's blurred photo shows a man holding a mug in a yellow window at the station.

lane_layout.text: Off the service lane are a lit gatehouse with a log board, a humming transformer hut, and steps down to a flooding cellar.

loop_note_in_cellar.text: A plastic sleeve with a folded note, first word LOOP, is taped above the tide line in the cellar.

note_loop_stays_up.text: The cellar note reads LOOP STAYS UP WHILE I DRAW BREATH, signed KX.

wren_soaked_cellar.text: Wren was soaked to the ribs escaping the flooding cellar.

wren_has_cellar_note.text: Wren has the cellar note in its sleeve in her pocket.

wren_fever.text: Wren caught a fever and spent three days in bed.

log_board_years.text: The gatehouse log board holds years of entries in one careful hand; the last is only hours old.

dog_patrols.text: A man with a dog patrols the compound at night.

log_loop_holding.text: The last forty log lines read LOOP HOLDING, STILL NO ANSWER, in tired handwriting.

person_tends_signal.text: A person tends the signal night after night, waiting for an answer.

log_for_m.text: The newest log page ends FOR M, STILL HOLDING.

wren_stole_log_page.text: Wren took the newest page of the log and keeps it folded small.

serviced_by_k_alder.text: The transformer hut's sticker shows monthly servicing by K. Alder for years, the last dated last month.

alder_stayed_on.text: Alder did not walk away when the county did; he still tends the station.

step_swept.text: The step under the lit window has been swept.

boots_on_step.text: The building is more cabin than station, with a rain barrel and a pair of boots on the step.

cedar_trunk.text: Grandpa kept the things he valued in a cedar trunk at the far end of the attic.

radio_shed_notes.text: Grandpa's radio shed holds a wall of pinned tuning notes untouched since he died.

trunk_contents.text: The trunk holds a water-stained logbook, a bundle of QSL cards, and unstamped envelopes tied with ribbon.

letters_to_kell.text: Grandpa's unsent letters are addressed to Relay KX and written to a man called Kell.

letter_keep_channel_open.text: The first letter begins: Kell, she may still be out there, so keep the channel open.

grandpa_knew_kell.text: Grandpa knew the man at the relay well and wrote to him for years without posting a word.

kell_alder_name.text: The man at the relay is Kell Alder.

kell_has_daughter.text: Kell Alder has a daughter from whom he is estranged.

letters_thirty.text: The bundle is about thirty envelopes thick.

grandpa_deliver_instruction.text: On the last envelope Grandpa wrote: if I am gone, take these out to KX by hand, because he needs to know somebody heard.

alder_operator.text: The operator at the headland relay is a man named Alder.

alder_still_transmitting.text: Grandpa's logbook keeps returning to ALDER STILL TRANSMITTING, WHY.

club_wont_talk.text: Nobody at the radio club will talk about Alder.

logbook_last_question.text: The logbook's last page, from the week Grandpa died, asks whether anybody will ever answer the poor man.

qsl_kx_alder.text: A heavier QSL card names the call sign KX ALDER, underlined twice by Grandpa.

kx_freq_matches_loop.text: Three cards give Relay KX's frequency, matching the loop; Grandpa logged it over a thousand nights.

no_listener_answered.text: As far as forty years of cards show, no listener on the coast ever answered Alder.

m_card_eleven_years.text: The newest card, eleven years old, reads: Heard KX again tonight, please do not tell him, M.

locked_cabinet.text: A padlocked filing cabinet in the shed holds Grandpa's letters; his screwdriver lies on the bench.

tuning_note_kx.text: A tuning note reads KX LOOP, HEADLAND RELAY, OPERATOR ALDER, DO NOT GIVE UP ON HIM.

grandpa_tried_reach_alder.text: Grandpa tried for years to reach Alder, who never answered, and ran out of time.

two_dots_slip.text: A slip in Grandpa's hand reads: KX, EVERY MIDNIGHT, TWO DOTS, NO REPLY YET.

wren_mother_catches.text: Wren's mother finds her in the wrecked shed and the shed is locked up.

loop_still_running.text: The loop is still running, faint and patient.

fence_pulled_away.text: Beside the chained gate the fence has pulled away from its post.

control_room.text: The lit room holds a console of dials, two reels of tape turning, a chair, and a steaming mug.

thirty_logbooks.text: A shelf holds about thirty logbooks with a year on every spine.

kell_nightly_thirty_years.text: Kell Alder is a person who has sat at that desk every night for thirty years sending the loop.

flashlight_approaching.text: A flashlight beam swings along the fence toward Wren.

wren_pencil_scrap.text: Wren has a pencil stub and a scrap of paper.

note_left_in_door.text: Wren wedged a note reading I HEAR YOU, signed W, in the relay station door.

flashlight_stopped_at_door.text: The flashlight stopped at the door where the note was and stayed there a long time.

kell_unaware_of_wren.text: Kell never knew Wren was at his window.

kell_found_note.text: Kell found Wren's note, walked the fence looking for her, and carries the paper in his shirt pocket.

county_says_decommissioned.text: The county website says the relay was decommissioned thirty years ago and has no staff.

wren_corkboard.text: Wren pins KELL ALDER, KX on the corkboard over her desk.

logbook_from_trunk.text: Grandpa's logbook, fetched down from the cedar trunk, lies by Wren's desk.

station_register.text: Tucked inside the logbook is the radio club's printed station register.

beat_might_be_time.text: The groups arrive on a not-quite-steady beat that might be time counted out loud.

loop_letter_m.text: The letter M recurs in the loop.

underlined_book.text: One other heavily underlined book of Grandpa's sits on the shelf above the desk.

msg_holding_for_m.text: Decoded with the register, the numbers say: STILL HOLDING THE CHANNEL OPEN FOR M.

count_going_down.text: Part of the broadcast is a count, and the count is going down.

underlined_is_tide_table.text: The underlined book is a tide table, and it decodes one cluster into a date and an hour.

clock_2340_tonight.text: The loop's countdown ends at twenty minutes to midnight tonight.

gaps_shrinking.text: The gaps between loop cycles shrink by a regular amount.

countdown_tonight.text: The loop is a countdown that ends tonight, a little before midnight.

rough_date_today.text: Wren's rough interval figures land on today on the calendar.

static_false_date.text: Run on plain static, Wren's method also produces a date.

voice_says_name_end.text: At about twenty to midnight the numbers stop, an old man's voice says a single name, then the channel is empty.

microfilm_library.text: The county library keeps the local paper on microfilm; the reading room shuts at seven.

okafor_at_marina.text: Old Mrs. Okafor mends nets at the marina and is said to remember everything and repeat almost nothing.

wren_barely_knows_okafor.text: Wren has never said more than hello to Mrs. Okafor.

wren_knows_okafor_well.text: Wren already knows Mrs. Okafor well.

closure_photo.text: A front page shows the county closing the relay, with one man standing apart.

kell_only_one_refused.text: Kell Alder, senior operator, was the only one of nine staff who refused the transfer inland.

keep_channel_open_quote.text: Asked why he stayed, Alder said: somebody has to keep the channel open.

closed_thirty_years.text: The relay was closed thirty years ago.

alder_would_not_go.text: A caption calls K. Alder the senior operator, the one who would not go.

neighbor_letter_nobody_listening.text: A neighbor's letter eleven years later complains the relay still hums and someone should tell that poor man nobody is listening.

okafor_demands_why.text: Mrs. Okafor will say nothing about Kell until Wren tells her why she wants to know.

okafor_told_truth.text: Wren told Mrs. Okafor the truth about the attic radio.

okafor_pins_cards.text: Mrs. Okafor has pinned a card to the pier board every month for thirty years saying the loop is real.

daughter_quarrel_left.text: Kell and his daughter had a bitter quarrel; she left on the morning bus and never wrote.

kell_vowed_channel.text: Kell swore before witnesses to keep a channel open until his daughter answered.

okafor_said_ring_marina.text: Mrs. Okafor told Wren to ring the marina, day or night, if the loop ever looks like stopping.

okafor_refuses_project.text: Mrs. Okafor will not hand a man's grief to a school project and sends Wren home.

girls_voice_on_air.text: A man has kept a girl's voice on the air for thirty years.

loop_two_tones_m.text: The loop opens with two long tones, dash dash, Morse for M.

morse_chart_lid.text: Grandpa taped an old Morse chart inside the radio's lid.

four_second_gap.text: After the falling tone there is a four-second gap of open air before the loop restarts.

kell_waits_for_answer.text: The gap is a pause to listen: the sender is waiting for an answer.

voice_is_kells_daughter.text: The voice reading the numbers is a girl, recorded years ago, who called the station's man Dad.

tone_lower_nightly.text: Each night the falling tone starts lower and the gap is shorter; the loop is running out of room.

wren_logged_week.text: Wren has a week of logged notes on the loop's starting tone.

marine_chart.text: Grandpa's marine chart of the headland is crowded with pencil letters for moorings and markers.

marin_name.text: Kell Alder's daughter is named Marin.

marin_vanished.text: Marin vanished from every local register thirty years ago with no forwarding address.

kell_sister.text: Kell Alder has a sister still living near the harbor.

marin_read_numbers.text: Marin used to read the station numbers for her father.

m_is_marin.text: M in the loop is Marin, Kell's daughter.

loop_is_apology.text: The loop is Kell's apology, calling his daughter home.

marin_address_west.text: Marin's last known address is in a town two ridges west.

sister_stopped_listening.text: Kell's sister stopped being able to listen to the loop years ago and is ashamed of it.

chart_m_mooring.text: On the chart Grandpa ringed an M twice beside a mooring inside the breakwater, dated thirty years ago.

mooring_kept.text: A brass plate on the old buoy reads Marin, a date, and HER MOORING IS KEPT.

chart_many_marks.text: The chart carries forty-one pencil marks; all lead back to the ringed M.

gale_forecast.text: The evening forecast warns of a gale on the headland.

archive_docs.text: The county archive has a relay maintenance sheet and an operating schedule, both printed by Wren.

single_power_cell.text: The relay runs on one sealed power cell, never replaced, whose rated life ended eleven years ago.

countdown_is_cell_life.text: The countdown measures how long the station's power has left to live.

final_tape_then_erase.text: The operating schedule's FINAL line reads PLAY TAPE 2, THEN ERASE ALL, dated today at twenty to midnight.

spring_tide_gale.text: Tonight's spring tide, with a gale behind it, tops out around twenty to midnight and floods the station yard.

wren_waterproof.text: Wren lays her waterproof jacket out ready.

tide_killed_power.text: The tide knocked out the power at the relay at twenty to midnight.

kell_tape_last_schedule.text: A tape of Kell's voice says: KX, this is your father, Marin; the cell will not carry another schedule; one hour left.

cell_failing.text: The station's power cell is failing and cannot carry another schedule.

kell_message_for_w.text: Kell recorded a message for the W who left three words: one answer, even from a stranger, was worth thirty years.

gale_arrives.text: The gale has arrived and rain is hammering the house.

grandpa_transmitter.text: Grandpa's transmitter sits under a dust sheet in the attic.

nobody_else_knows.text: Nobody but Wren knows the station dies tonight.

others_know_tonight.text: Someone besides Wren and Kell knows the station dies tonight.

yard_flooded.text: The relay yard is a sheet of black water.

service_road_back.text: A sheltered service road curves round to the back of the compound.

door_ajar.text: Across the open yard a door stands ajar with warm light spilling out.

kell_at_mast.text: The control room is empty; Kell is out at the foot of the mast fighting a loose cable.

kell_inside_console.text: Kell sits inside at the console with a heavy headset on, his back to the window.

erase_tape_strip.text: A tape strip on the console reads AFTER LAST SEND, ERASE.

hold_switch.text: A guarded HOLD switch on the console would stop the sending and the erasing.

circled_number.text: An address book beside Kell's telephone has one number circled so often the paper shines.

circled_is_marin.text: The circled number is the one person the last message was always meant for.

phone_patch.text: A patch cord runs from the telephone into the console, so a call can carry the message.

kell_sorry_message.text: Kell's last message: Marin, I kept your voice on the air so that you would always know the way home; I am sorry.

tape_erased.text: The tape plays its last and erases itself.

marin_answers.text: Marin answers, and father and daughter are connected.

kell_returns.text: Kell comes in from the storm to find Wren at his console.

tapes_saved.text: The thirty years of tapes are saved, not erased.

second_cell_terminals.text: Two bare terminals under the desk wait for a second cell that was never fitted.

station_stable.text: With Grandpa's battery spliced in, the station will run for hours.

club_night_number.text: The radio club's night number is taped to Kell's telephone.

club_rallies.text: Radio club members arrive with trucks and a generator and take over the rescue.

one_word_saved.text: Wren's phone recording saved one word of the message: Marin.

kell_marin_not_listening.text: Kell says Marin is not listening and tonight he is only saying goodbye.

kell_speaks_live.text: Kell speaks into the microphone live for the first time in thirty years.

marin_still_listening.text: Marin never quite stopped tuning in.

others_promised_kell.text: The harbormaster, the minister and Kell's sister all once promised him Marin was listening.

grandpa_answered_two_dots.text: Grandpa sent two dots every midnight for twenty years; Kell took it for a fault in the set.

wren_eight_miles.text: Wren's attic is about eight miles from the relay.

steel_door_bolted.text: The back door is steel and bolted from the inside, beside a small window.

wren_unlicensed.text: Wren has no transmitting license and Grandpa never let her key the transmitter.

net_emergency_line.text: Grandpa's club card gives the county radio net's emergency line.

power_pencil_mark.text: Grandpa always kept the transmitter's power at a pencil mark, short of a red band.

silent_carrier.text: Someone answers Wren's call with a bare, silent carrier.

transmitter_burned.text: Pushed into the red band, the transmitter burned out.

neighbor_heard.text: A woman two streets over heard Wren on her kitchen radio and knew the Callahan frequency.

net_relays_message.text: Stations across the county pass the message for Marin Alder onward.

net_press_one.text: The net's recording offers press one for danger to life or property, or a message heard at six.

woman_two_ridges_west.text: A woman two ridges west who will not give a call sign keeps asking what the message says.

wren_never_learns.text: Wren never learns how it ends between Kell and Marin.

west_listener_eleven_winters.text: A listener two ridges west has asked after the station every winter for eleven years.

coast_guard_number.text: The coast guard auxiliary's number is printed on the tide table.

grandpa_address_book.text: Grandpa's address book holds forty years of radio friends.

okafor_has_key.text: Mrs. Okafor has a key to the relay's back door; she has left soup on its step for thirty years.

number_six_years.text: Kell has had the circled number for six years without dialing it.

cg_at_relay.text: A coast guard crew reaches the relay and finds Kell elderly, uninjured and annoyed.

missing_relative_file.text: The auxiliary opens a missing-relative file for Marin Alder.

tapes_ruined_kell_unhurt.text: The sea floods the relay; Kell is found unhurt among thirty years of ruined tape.

eight_transferred.text: Eight relay men in Grandpa's book are marked TRANSFERRED INLAND.

ruiz_stayed.text: A relay man named Ruiz stayed local, across the bay; he did not transfer.

ruiz_has_keys.text: Ruiz still has keys to the relay and knew Kell would one day set the last schedule.

ruiz_splices_cell.text: Ruiz wires a spare cell across the dying one while Kell holds the count.

ruiz_watches_lamp.text: Ruiz has watched the relay's mast lamp from his kitchen every night.

n_open.event: Sleepless Wren switches on her late grandfather's attic radio and hears the looping numbers again.

n_shelf.event: Wren eyes Grandpa's untouched spare battery and headset and allows herself to take one.

n_shelf_battery.event: She packs the heavy spare battery.

n_shelf_headset.event: She puts on the headset and the voice comes startlingly close.

n_start.event: Three leads pull at her: coordinates, the relay station, Grandpa's logbook.

r_coord_1.event: The numbers plot to the harbor and the ridge water tower; she must pick one.

r_coord_harbor.event: At the sleeping harbor: the harbormaster's hut, the tide-gauge shed, the notice-board.

r_coord_notice.event: A fresh index card on the board says the loop is real.

r_coord_notice2.event: The card's frequency matches the loop and its ink is still damp; is it meant for her?

r_coord_notice3.event: She takes the card, tunes to it, and the signal points north to the headland.

e_coord_notice.event: She leaves the card; someone keeps replacing it, nobody comes, and the loop ends.

r_coord_harbor_ask.event: Mr. Pell says the loop came off the old headland relay and won't name the man behind it.

r_coord_harbor_shed.event: Through the shed window a receiver blinks with the loop; the door could be shoved.

r_coord_shed_in.event: Inside, a card reads RELAY KX: the shed is only an ear for a signal further out.

e_coord_shed_leave.event: She copies the frequency and goes home; Grandpa had marked it on his dial and never said a word; the loop ends.

r_coord_tower.event: The water tower rebroadcasts the signal; a bad ladder and a service box offer two ways in.

r_coord_climb.event: She freezes on the ladder but sees a cable running to the relay on the point.

r_coord_base.event: The rusted service box could be pried open; stenciled arrows point along the ridge.

r_coord_base_in.event: A tag shows the tower is a repeater for KX on the headland.

r_coord_base_out.event: She follows reflective arrows along the ridge toward the headland.

r_coord_beat.event: Walking the headland track, she understands the numbers point to the relay on the point.

r_coord_close.event: The relay is lit; she creeps down to the lit window.

r_relay_1.event: She bikes to the relay's chained gate; a coast path and a service lane lead on.

r_re_path.event: On the windy coast path she finds a fence gap and a clear view of the mast.

r_re_gap.event: Inside the compound, a RELAY KX sign and signs that the place is tended.

e_re_photo.event: She photographs the mast and turns back; one photo shows a man with a mug; the loop stops next night.

r_re_lane.event: Down the flooded lane: a gatehouse log board, a transformer hut, a cellar doorway.

r_re_cellar.event: In the flooding cellar a note sleeve begins LOOP.

r_re_cellar2.event: The note promises LOOP STAYS UP WHILE I DRAW BREATH, KX, as the water rises.

r_re_cellar3.event: She salvages the note and barely escapes the surge, soaked.

e_re_cellar.event: She flees the cellar with the words in her head, catches a fever, and the loop is gone when she recovers.

r_re_gatehouse.event: In the warm gatehouse a years-long log board; a dog starts barking.

r_re_log.event: The log says LOOP HOLDING, STILL NO ANSWER; a person tends the signal; the dog walker leaves.

r_re_scrap.event: She runs with the newest page: FOR M, STILL HOLDING.

r_re_hut.event: The transformer hut's sticker shows K. Alder has serviced it monthly for years.

r_relay_beat.event: In the rain she sees one lit window and a swept step under the mast; the voice comes from there.

r_relay_close.event: She reaches the lit window; it is a cabin with boots on the step.

r_notes_1.event: She goes looking for Grandpa's logbook: the cedar trunk or the radio shed.

r_no_trunk.event: The trunk holds a logbook, QSL cards and unsent letters.

r_no_letters.event: The unsent letters are to Kell at Relay KX: she may still be out there, keep the channel open.

r_no_letters2.event: The letter names Kell Alder and pleads for his daughter; reading on feels like trespass.

r_no_letters3.event: She reads on: years of letters urging Kell Alder not to give up; she keeps one.

e_no_letters.event: She leaves the letters unread; later finds Grandpa's plea to deliver them, but the loop is gone.

r_no_book.event: The logbook tracks the KX loop: ALDER STILL TRANSMITTING, WHY, and a last unanswered question.

r_no_cards.event: Among the QSL cards one names KX ALDER.

r_no_freq.event: Three cards confirm Relay KX and Alder on the loop's frequency; nobody ever answered him.

e_no_cards_end.event: She sorts all the cards till three; the newest is from M; by the time it means anything the loop is gone.

r_no_shed.event: The shed: hundreds of tuning notes, and a padlocked letter cabinet.

r_no_tuning.event: A double-circled note: KX LOOP, OPERATOR ALDER, DO NOT GIVE UP ON HIM.

e_no_locked.event: Forcing the cabinet topples it; she is caught, but finds a slip: KX, EVERY MIDNIGHT, TWO DOTS.

r_notes_beat.event: She realizes Grandpa knew of Alder and kept silent; she sets out before one.

r_notes_close.event: She bikes to the relay, slips through the fence, and reaches the lit window.

n_b1.event: Through the window: a warm control room, a license for Kell Alder of Station KX, thirty logbooks; a flashlight approaches.

n_b1_note.event: She wedges I HEAR YOU, W in the door and flees; the flashlight stops at the door.

n_b1_slip.event: She backs away unseen and watches a stooped figure sit at the desk.

n_b1_echo.event: Next day she pins KELL ALDER, KX up; the county says the relay has no staff.

n_b1_choice.event: Crack the numbers or ask the town about Kell Alder.

m_numbers_1.event: With Grandpa's logbook and the station register, she weighs a book cipher against timing the beat.

m_num_cipher.event: The register yields HOLDING, ANSWER and a recurring M, then stalls on one cluster.

m_num_cracked.event: One page off; the message reads STILL HOLDING THE CHANNEL OPEN FOR M, with a falling count.

m_num_book2.event: The tide table decodes one cluster into a date and hour, the rest to rubbish.

e_num_gibberish.event: She grinds the tide table against everything past one in the morning; the loop is gone; the date was the message.

m_num_time.event: Timing the cycles, she finds the gaps shrinking regularly.

m_num_intervals.event: Her curve hits zero tonight before midnight: a countdown.

m_num_pattern.event: Rough figures land on today; she doubts herself.

m_num_countdown.event: She circles today: the loop is a countdown ending tonight, threaded with M.

e_num_giveup.event: Static also gives a date, so she bins it; at twenty to midnight a man's voice says a name and the loop ends.

m_who_1.event: Library microfilm or old Mrs. Okafor at the marina?

m_who_film.event: A front page on the relay's closing shows one man apart; the library is closing.

m_who_article.event: The man is Kell Alder, the only one of nine who refused transfer: somebody has to keep the channel open.

m_who_photo.event: Her photos show K. Alder, the one who would not go, and a letter saying nobody is listening.

m_who_okafor.event: Mrs. Okafor demands to know why Wren asks about Kell.

m_who_story.event: Told the truth, Okafor reveals her pier cards, Kell's daughter, the quarrel, his vow; ring the marina if it stops.

e_who_warn.event: Okafor refuses a school project and leaves Wren with a worse question about a girl's voice.

n_b2.event: At the radio, the two tones are Morse M and the four-second gap is a pause for an answer.

n_b2_under.event: Through the headset an older recording bleeds through: the reader is a girl who calls the man Dad.

n_b2_echo.event: Her week of logs shows the tone starting lower each night: the loop is running out.

n_b2_choice.event: Two questions: who is M, and what is the count running down to?

mm_listener_1.event: M could be a person in family records or a place on Grandpa's chart.

mm_list_family.event: Records show Kell's one child, Marin, vanished thirty years ago, and a sister near the harbor.

mm_list_daughter.event: A forum post: Kell's girl Marin read the numbers, left after a row; M is Marin and the loop an apology.

mm_list_sister.event: Kell's sister confirms M is Marin, gives an address two ridges west, urges speed.

mm_list_place.event: On the chart a twice-ringed M sits by a mooring inside the breakwater.

mm_list_map.event: The buoy's plate reads Marin, HER MOORING IS KEPT: M is a person.

e_list_deadend.event: She works through every chart mark and misses the end: a man's voice says a name, then nothing.

mm_count_1.event: Follow the falling line to zero, or check it against the tide table and forecast.

mm_count_time.event: The line hits zero at twenty to midnight tonight; two archive documents remain.

mm_count_extrap.event: The maintenance sheet: one dying cell; the countdown is the station's remaining life.

mm_count_clock.event: The schedule's FINAL line: PLAY TAPE 2, THEN ERASE ALL, today at twenty to midnight.

mm_count_tide.event: A spring tide and a gale both peak near twenty to midnight at the headland.

mm_count_warn.event: Trusting the tide: the station will drown as the count reaches zero.

e_count_wait.event: She waits for daylight; the tide killed the relay's power overnight.

n_b3.event: At 22:40 a tape of Kell breaks in: Marin, the cell is dying, one hour left, then goodbye.

n_b3_note.event: The tape adds a message for the W who left three words in his door.

n_b3_echo.event: The gale arrives; she thinks of the small warm room and the man counting down his station.

n_b3_choice.event: Fifty-nine minutes: ride, transmit, or phone; nobody else knows.

f_station_1.event: She rides to the flooded station with nine minutes left: fence or service road.

f_st_fence.event: Inside the yard: the open way across, or the sheltered long way by the sheds.

f_st_control.event: The empty control room: countdown, AFTER LAST SEND, ERASE, a HOLD switch, a circled number, a failing cell.

f_st_answer.event: She grasps the plan: dial the circled number to let it play, or HOLD to save the tapes.

e_st_reunite.event: The message plays down the line to Marin and erases; Kell walks in and Wren hands him the phone.

e_st_archive.event: She throws HOLD; nothing sent or erased; Kell sees and decides to stay.

f_st_power.event: The cell is dying; two bare terminals wait for a second cell.

f_st_spliced.event: Grandpa's battery holds the station for hours; time for more than one thing.

e_st_stabilize.event: She calls the radio club; trucks arrive, HOLD is thrown, someone calls west.

e_st_both.event: She throws HOLD and dials Marin, playing the tape by hand; Kell hears his daughter.

e_st_record.event: She nurses the cell; it dies on one word, Marin, saved on her phone; the battery was left behind.

e_st_hesitate.event: She takes the long way and arrives one minute late; the tapes erase.

f_st_road.event: At the back, Kell sits in his headset behind a bolted steel door and a small window.

f_st_alder.event: Kell lets her in but says Marin is not listening; tonight is only goodbye.

e_st_alder_send.event: Wren admits she cannot promise; Kell goes live and Marin answers.

e_st_alder_refuse.event: A false promise closes him; the tape plays to an empty sky and erases; they sit together.

e_st_note.event: She owns the note; Kell learns Grandpa answered with two dots for years, goes live, and Marin answers.

e_st_wait.event: She hammers the steel door unheard; the goodbye plays and the lamp goes out.

f_relay_1.event: Under the dust sheet, Grandpa's transmitter; she has no license; the net's emergency line is on the wall.

f_re_rig.event: She warms the set and patches the loop out with her voice; the power knob runs into a red band.

f_re_boost.event: Sending at the pencil mark, she gets a silent carrier while the phone rings downstairs.

e_re_answer.event: She coaxes the carrier; Marin's voice answers, the same as the loop; Wren gives them the channel.

e_re_neighbor.event: A neighbor's brother, the net controller, spreads the message; strangers carry Marin's name on.

e_re_fuse.event: Into the red band: ten seconds out, then the set burns out; a neighbor wants the rest.

f_re_club.event: The net's recording: press one for danger, or leave a message for six a.m.

f_re_net.event: The controller puts out a call for Marin Alder; a woman two ridges west asks what it says.

e_re_found.event: Patched through, the woman is Marin; she read those numbers at seventeen; Kell answers live.

e_re_log.event: They log twenty-three stations; the net keeps calling Marin after the loop stops.

e_re_message.event: She leaves a message; at six the controller wishes she had pressed one: a listener west had been asking for years.

f_help_1.event: Whom to wake: the coast guard, a relay man from Grandpa's book, or the marina.

f_he_okafor.event: Okafor drives her out and opens the back door with Kell's key.

e_he_okafor.event: Okafor makes Kell dial the circled number; Marin answers.

f_he_cg.event: The coast guard officer wants a location, then the emergency.

f_he_act.event: Location, hazard, time: a crew reaches Kell before the spring tide; one job before the tide tops.

e_he_escort.event: The clerk finds Marin's number; the chief puts her through to her father.

e_he_safe.event: Sandbags and a generator; Kell throws HOLD; a missing-relative file is opened for Marin.

e_he_dismiss.event: Told the whole story, the officer files it under curiosities; the sea floods the relay.

f_he_colleague.event: Grandpa's book: eight relay men transferred inland, and Ruiz, who stayed.

f_he_join.event: Ruiz drives her to the relay and tells her to stay in the truck.

e_he_complete.event: All three work together; Ruiz splices a cell, Kell holds, Wren dials the circled number; Marin answers.

e_he_takeover.event: She waits in the truck and never learns the end; the door is open in daylight.

e_he_dead.event: The inland numbers fail; the seventh points to Ruiz, too late; the lamp went out at twenty to midnight.

payoff_sites.shows: Grandpa's JUST IN CASE battery splices in and holds the dying station for hours
without the battery the cell dies on one word, and the left-behind battery is remembered
the headset reveals the reading voice is a girl calling the station man Dad
Kell's last tape adds a message for the W who left three words in his door
owning the note unlocks Grandpa's two dots and Kell going live to Marin
Mrs. Okafor answers at once, drives Wren out, and has a key to Kell's door

e_coord_notice.gift: the card was real and someone keeps it up; deferring to an unknown reader cost her the loop

e_coord_shed_leave.gift: Grandpa's pencil tick shows he heard it too; a sensible plan for later was too late

e_re_photo.gift: proof that a man lives out there, and the lesson that the loop will not wait for daylight

e_re_cellar.gift: the promise LOOP STAYS UP WHILE I DRAW BREATH, and the cost of a cold night in the sea

e_no_letters.gift: Grandpa's plea to take the letters to KX by hand: some grief is meant to be delivered

e_no_cards_end.gift: the M card, an eleven-year-old clue that M was listening, found too late

e_no_locked.gift: the two-dots slip: Grandpa was sending to KX every midnight; force cost her the wall she skipped

e_num_gibberish.gift: the date and hour were the whole message; perfectionism spent the deadline

e_num_giveup.gift: proof the date was real; skepticism at the wrong moment let the loop end

e_who_warn.gift: Okafor's question about a girl's voice kept on air thirty years; a cover story closes doors

e_list_deadend.gift: the only mark Grandpa ringed twice was the answer; thoroughness missed the end

e_count_wait.gift: the tide was the clock; waiting for daylight was one night too long

e_st_reunite.gift: the message reaches Marin as Kell planned and Wren hands him the phone

e_st_archive.gift: nothing erased: thirty years kept for Marin, and Kell decides to stay

e_st_stabilize.gift: the battery buys time and a whole community comes; the waiting is shared

e_st_both.gift: both at once: tapes saved and Marin on the line, calling for her dad

e_st_record.gift: one saved word, Marin, and the lesson of the battery left JUST IN CASE

e_st_hesitate.gift: the straight way across was only thirty yards; caution cost the last minute

e_st_alder_send.gift: honest not-knowing persuades Kell to go live, and Marin answers

e_st_alder_refuse.gift: a false promise closes him; honesty would have opened him; quiet company remains

e_st_note.gift: the note links Wren, Grandpa's two dots and Kell; Marin answers with two clicks

e_st_wait.gift: the window was glass and six steps away; force at the wrong door

e_re_answer.gift: Marin answers the carrier and Wren gives father and daughter the channel

e_re_neighbor.gift: the message spreads coast-wide through strangers carrying Marin's name

e_re_fuse.gift: ten seconds on air and a burned set: Grandpa's pencil mark was not timidity

e_re_found.gift: Marin, who read those numbers at seventeen, is found two ridges west and Kell answers live

e_re_log.gift: a hundred hands carry the message on; Wren will never know which one reaches Marin

e_re_message.gift: a listener two ridges west had asked for years; property was in danger, press one

e_he_okafor.gift: Okafor's trust brings Wren in and makes Kell dial the number he never dialed

e_he_escort.gift: the coast guard finds Marin and puts her through to her father

e_he_safe.gift: the station and tapes are saved and a search opens for Marin; place, danger, hour first

e_he_dismiss.gift: Kell survives but thirty years of tape are lost; next time start with the tide

e_he_complete.gift: it takes all three: Ruiz, Kell and Wren reunite father and daughter

e_he_takeover.gift: the end happened thirty yards away; some things you must hear from the man himself

e_he_dead.gift: Ruiz was the one to call; eight chances were worse than one
